exposure: use of intrauterine inflated Foley's catheter balloon
outcome: Blood transfusion requirements (crystalloids, colloids, packed red blood cells)
Need for bilateral internal iliac artery ligation
cohort: 78 women who underwent elective caesarean section for abnormally invasive placenta previa (40 with intrauterine inflated Foley's catheter balloon and 38 without)
finding: In this retrospective case-control study of 78 women undergoing caesarean section for abnormally invasive placenta previa, the use of an intrauterine inflated Foley's catheter balloon was associated with reduced blood loss, blood transfusion requirements, and the need for bilateral internal iliac artery ligation.
mod_finding: This study focuses on women undergoing cesarean section for abnormally invasive placenta previa.
